summary: OWASP Phase 2 fully validated against preview backend — 21/21 pytest pass. (1) IDOR/ownership on sessions chain: as Coach B (newly registered), PUT /api/sessions/{id}/complete on Coach A's session returns 404, POST /api/microcycles?mesocycle_id= returns 404, POST /api/sessions?microcycle_id= returns 404, POST /api/mesocycles?macrocycle_id= returns 404; Coach A can complete his own session with 200. (2) NoSQL injection blocked by Pydantic typing: POST /api/auth/login with {"email":{"$ne":null},"password":"x"} -> 422; same for object password -> 422 (no 500). (3) XSS public share: POST /api/graphic-plan/share with plan_name='' + image_b64='javascript:alert(2)' creates share; GET /api/graphic-plan/shared/{id} returns HTML with the plan_name escaped (<script>alert(1)</script>), raw
critical_code_review_comments: routes/sessions.py::_assert_meso_owner returns 'Mesocycle not found' both when meso doesn't exist and when caller is not the owner — good (no info leak). Same pattern in _assert_micro_owner. OK.
routes/sessions.py::complete_session does an UPDATE without idempotency check; it always returns 200 even if the session was already completed. Cosmetic — consider returning the new state or 304.

routes/graphic_plan_share.py: html.escape applies to plan_name; image_b64 only kept if startswith('data:image/'). Good. Suggest also enforcing a Content-Security-Policy meta inside the rendered HTML page (defense in depth, currently relying only on server-set headers).

core/models.py UserLogin uses EmailStr — that is what blocks {"$ne":null} with 422. Confirmed working. Recommend extending the same EmailStr/str type strictness to any other endpoint that previously relied on the (now-removed) body-buffering middleware (e.g., search/filter endpoints accepting dicts as raw Body).

routes/auth.py register rate-limit is 5/minute — fine, but consider also brute-force/lockout on /auth/register email enumeration (currently returns 400 'Email already registered' which is an information disclosure).
server.py: CSP keeps 'unsafe-inline' for script-src (CRA inline runtime) — planned trade-off; document or migrate to nonces in next phase.
